source.inspection: Original-resolution raster viewed directly; pixel dimensions and file hash read. No application code, application output, archived expected results, or existing feature extraction was inspected. The PDF was not read.
source.coordinate_convention: Image origin at upper left; x increases rightwards and y downwards. All pixel coordinates below are approximate visual readings.

series_identity.blue_markers: Soil moisture (% water content), right axis
series_identity.warning: Blue-marker positions are not Delta-SNR observations. Scatter darkness is printed overplotting, not a labelled quantile, median, or statistical mode.

caveats: UTC is the candidate coordinate convention; the raster itself labels the horizontal axis only as Time and does not explicitly specify a timezone.
The inferred right boundary is approximately 2017-05-01, but no labelled May tick is visible.
Do not confuse the small axis-calibration uncertainty with the much larger uncertainty in selecting a central-darkness band.

central_darkness_candidate_boxes.interpretation: Broad envelope for the most visually concentrated central dark portions of the daily scatter columns. It does not enclose every dark pixel or a defined probability mass.
Broad envelope for the central dark concentration; the conspicuous downward April-16 plume is a separate feature, not part of the central-band estimate.
Broad envelope for the central dark concentration. Blue soil-moisture markers partially cover this same visual area and must not be counted as scatter evidence.

central_darkness_uncertainty_and_validit.period_selection: Three equal seven-day review windows chosen by this reviewer to represent early, middle, and late April; these windows are not defined in the source raster.
central_darkness_uncertainty_and_validit.qualitative_observation: The central dark concentration appears modestly higher later in April, but the candidate bands overlap substantially and individual daily columns vary.
central_darkness_uncertainty_and_validit.conditions: Use only as approximate image-derived descriptive envelopes with reviewer uncertainty. Do not name the box centers modes, medians, quantiles, or independent numerical ground truth.
central_darkness_uncertainty_and_validit.scientific_regression_limit: These boxes can support a coarse source-consistency check. Alone they cannot validate the scientific aggregation, sample counts, distribution quantiles, a precise month-long change, or a required ordering of early/middle/late statistical modes. No distinct numerical modal estimate was extracted.

negative_excursion_candidate.interpretation: A narrow, conspicuously dark downward plume is visible near the middle of April 16. This box contains a clear negative portion of that feature and deliberately describes its presence rather than its minimum.
negative_excursion_candidate.minimum_reason: The plume thins towards the lower plot boundary at -20 dB. The raster does not establish an uncensored minimum, and -18 dB is a candidate box boundary, not an asserted minimum observation.
negative_excursion_candidate.confidence: High for the existence and approximate date of a strong negative excursion; lower for tail extent and unsuitable for recovering an exact minimum or count.

strongest_source_features: Broad positive central concentration with substantial distributional spread.
Blue points belong to an independently scaled moisture series.
do_not_assert: A source-provided numerical median, quantile, or statistical mode.
An observed minimum equal to the -20 dB plot boundary.
A precise monotonic progression of central values across the month.
A scatter-sample count, causal moisture relationship, or scientific equivalence solely from image darkness.
